title: feat(export): YouTube preset exports 1440p or 4K (NIW2-564)
body:
Closes NIW2-564 — https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-564/youtube-export-1440p-4k-upscale-for-sharper-uploads

## Why
YouTube re-encodes 1440p and 4K uploads far better than 1080p ones, even for viewers watching at 1080p. A 1916×1048 @ 48 fps screen recording looked soft uploaded through the 1080p YouTube preset; the same video upscaled to 2560×1440 (ffmpeg lanczos, CRF 16) and re-uploaded looked clearly sharper. Uploading 1080p to YouTube has no upside, so the YouTube preset now produces 1440p or 4K. Stays on mediabunny/WebCodecs (ADR 0001): no ffmpeg in the build.

## What changed
- **Presets** (`export-presets.ts`, `shared/types/export-preset.ts`): `youtube` (1920×1080) → `youtube-1440` (2560×1440) and `youtube-4k` (3840×2160). Fit with black padding, source frame rate, 2 s keyframes, fast start. Video bitrate from [YouTube's upload guide](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/1722171), SDR top of range: 1440p 16 / 24 Mbps, 2160p 45 / 68 Mbps (≤30 / >30 fps). AAC 384 kbps, falling back to 256 / 192 / 128k if the encoder refuses.
- **Default variant**: `defaultYoutubePreset(source)` → 4K when fitting into 2560×1440 would shrink the source, else 1440p.
- **Export sheet**: one YouTube row with a 1440p / 4K segmented control (same pattern as Fill / Fit). Collapsed hint shows "16:9 · 1440p" / "16:9 · 4K". No amber heavy-size styling or chip on this row: bigger than the recording is the point. New microcopy, en + es.
- **Legacy sidecars**: `youtube` normalizes to `youtube-1440` for display; new `ENCODE_REVISION` entries keep an old export from ever counting as "already exported".
- **Upscale quality**: the Fit/Fill framer and the zoom crop already used `imageSmoothingQuality = "high"`; slides (`drawContained`) did not, and now do. This is not what improved the YouTube result — the 1440p/4K upload is.
- Docs: `backlog/export-presets.md`.

## Product concept
One row with a resolution choice instead of two YouTube rows (GPT-6.1 Sol product review, owner-approved): pick the destination first, then the variant.

## Verification
- `bun run verify` (lint, oxfmt, build, types, unit tests): exit 0, 2976 tests passed.
- The `/verify` Electron proof scenario and the e2e suite were **not** run locally (owner-machine rule); CI covers e2e on release candidates.
- **Not verified at runtime**: whether Chromium's AAC encoder accepts 384 kbps (fallback list is unit-tested), and whether VideoToolbox accepts 3840×2160 at 68 Mbps through WebCodecs (the existing encoder probe should fall back).

## How to test it yourself
1. `bun run dev`, open a recording made on a 1080p monitor (e.g. `recording-2026-10-30-01-01-57`) in the editor → **Export**.
2. In the Post group there is **one** YouTube row; its hint reads "16:9 · 1440p" and the size column shows 2560×1440. No amber size.
3. Select it: a **Resolution 1440p / 4K** control appears. Switch to 4K → dimensions become 3840×2160 and the MB estimate grows. Switch back.
4. Export at 1440p. When done: `ffprobe -v error -show_entries stream=codec_type,width,height,avg_frame_rate,bit_rate -of compact=p=0 "<exported file>"` → 2560×1440, source fps (48), video ≈ 24 Mbps, audio ≈ 384000 (or a lower fallback — tell me which).
5. Export the same recording at 4K → 3840×2160 and it finishes without an encoder error.
6. Upload the 1440p file to YouTube; once the 1440p option appears, compare text sharpness with the old upload.
7. A Retina/HiDPI recording (larger than 2560×1440) opens the sheet with 4K preselected.
